sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.zh: 我凌晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空探索七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60份超级圣代。

sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最强的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来致力于帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 现在订阅可享受特别优惠，网址是 nytimes.com/subscribe。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is a daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今日话题。

sentences.en: A major new study has revealed in staggering ways just how much elite college admissions in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 一项重大的新研究以惊人的方式揭示了美国精英大学的录取过程在多大程度上，

sentences.en: systematically favor the rich and the super rich.
sentences.zh: 系统性地偏袒富人和超级富豪。

sentences.en: My colleague, David Leonhardt, walks us through the data and explains why the study is fueling calls to abandon long-standing practices like legacy admissions.
sentences.zh: 我的同事大卫·莱昂哈特将带我们梳理这些数据，并解释为什么这项研究引发了废除诸如校友子女优先录取等长期做法的呼声。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, July 27th.
sentences.zh: 今天是7月27日，星期四。

sentences.en: David, welcome back to The Daily.
sentences.zh: 大卫，欢迎回到《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: David, after the Supreme Court struck down race-based affirmative action in college admissions a few weeks ago, said it was unconstitutional,
sentences.zh: 大卫，几周前最高法院裁定大学录取中基于种族的平权行动违宪后，

sentences.en: a lot of people's attention quickly turned to other features of the college admissions process that feel, in a way, like alternative forms of affirmative action and preference,
sentences.zh: 许多人的注意力迅速转向了大学录取过程中其他感觉像是平权行动和优待替代形式的特征，

sentences.en: giving people a clear set of advantages in the process.
sentences.zh: 在录取过程中为某些人提供了明显的优势。

sentences.en: And a lot of those people started asking, why aren't we talking about all the ways that college admissions favor the privileged?
sentences.zh: 很多人开始问，为什么我们不讨论大学录取偏袒特权阶层的所有方式呢？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think that makes sense because college admissions are about to change more than they have in a long time.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很有道理，因为大学录取即将发生长久以来最大的变化。

sentences.en: And so it makes sense for colleges and for society as a whole to ask, well, what features of the current system should remain and what features should change?
sentences.zh: 因此，大学乃至整个社会去思考当前制度中哪些特征应该保留，哪些应该改变，是合情合理的。

sentences.en: Not just affirmative action, but really the whole process.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是平权行动，而是整个录取过程。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: And in the midst of that debate comes a study.
sentences.zh: 而在这场辩论中，一项研究出现了。

sentences.en: And we get a lot of studies in the world of journalism.
sentences.zh: 在新闻界，我们经常收到各种研究报告。

sentences.en: But this study stood out.
sentences.zh: 但这项研究脱颖而出。

sentences.en: And it's what we want to talk with you about because it seems to offer a really authoritative, perhaps even the most authoritative ever look,
sentences.zh: 这就是我们想和你讨论的原因，因为它似乎提供了一个非常权威，甚至可能是史上最权威的视角，

sentences.en: at how systems of advantage for those with a lot of advantages already play out in the college admissions process.
sentences.zh: 审视那些已经拥有大量优势的人，其优势体系是如何在大学录取过程中发挥作用的。

sentences.en: So, David, tell us about this study.
sentences.zh: 那么，大卫，给我们介绍一下这项研究吧。

sentences.en: I do think it's the clearest look we've gotten behind the scenes at college admissions at these elite schools.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为这是我们迄今为止对这些精英学校大学录取幕后情况最清晰的观察。

sentences.en: And the reason is that it combined admissions records, internal admissions records, that several of these colleges gave the researchers access to with tax returns,
sentences.zh: 原因在于，它将几所大学提供给研究人员的内部录取记录与纳税申报表结合了起来，

sentences.en: which gives us hard data on who it is that is applying to these schools.
sentences.zh: 这为我们提供了关于谁在申请这些学校的硬数据。

sentences.en: And that allows us, in a way that we really haven't before, to get a very clear sense of who's applying, who's getting in and who's going.
sentences.zh: 这使我们能够以一种前所未有的方式，非常清楚地了解谁在申请、谁被录取以及谁最终入学。

sentences.en: And I've gotten to know this study really well because I've been reporting on these same issues for 20 years
sentences.zh: 我对这项研究非常了解，因为我报道这些议题已经20年了，

sentences.en: and talking to these researchers who are at Harvard and Brown who did it.
sentences.zh: 并且一直与哈佛和布朗大学进行这项研究的研究人员保持交流。

sentences.en: And I'm actually an informal unpaid advisor to them.
sentences.zh: 实际上，我还是他们非正式的无薪顾问。

sentences.en: I give them thoughts about what are the questions that those of us who aren't economists want answered by data like this.
sentences.zh: 我会向他们提出一些像我们这些非经济学家希望通过此类数据得到解答的问题。

sentences.en: And I really do think, after years of writing about this, that this has given me and all of us a better sense
sentences.zh: 在撰写相关报道多年后，我确实认为这让我以及我们所有人更好地了解了，

sentences.en: of what actually happens inside admissions offices than we've had before.
sentences.zh: 招生办公室内部到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: And so with all this information, what did the researchers who did this study find?
sentences.zh: 那么，有了所有这些信息，进行这项研究的研究人员发现了什么？

sentences.en: What's the headline result?
sentences.zh: 核心结论是什么？

sentences.en: I think the headline result is that we live in an extremely unequal society and college admissions in some ways makes it more unequal.
sentences.zh: 我认为核心结论是我们生活在一个极度不平等的社会中，而大学录取在某些方面加剧了这种不平等。

sentences.en: So affluent kids are, on average, much more qualified than less affluent kids.
sentences.zh: 所以，富裕家庭的孩子平均而言比不那么富裕的孩子更有竞争力。

sentences.en: They have better academic qualifications by any measure, grades, SAT scores, essays.
sentences.zh: 无论从什么标准来看，他们的学术资质都更好，包括成绩、SAT分数和论文。

sentences.en: And so, of course, because colleges need to think about which students are prepared to do the work, colleges are going to end up admitting more affluent students for those reasons.
sentences.zh: 因此，由于大学需要考虑哪些学生准备好完成学业，出于这些原因，大学最终会录取更多的富裕学生。

sentences.en: And yet, even on top of that, colleges give large advantages in admissions to privileged kids over similarly qualified middle and low-income kids.
sentences.zh: 然而，即便如此，大学在录取时仍给予特权阶层孩子比同等资质的中低收入家庭孩子更大的优势。

sentences.en: And it's that last thing.
sentences.zh: 正是最后这一点，

sentences.en: It's that idea that when you're looking at two kids who have similar grades, similar test scores, similar academic qualifications,
sentences.zh: 即当你审视两个成绩、考试分数和学术资质相似的孩子时，

sentences.en: that the affluent kid, and particularly the very affluent kid, is nonetheless more likely to get in, it's that idea that has caused this study to get so much attention.
sentences.zh: 富裕家庭的孩子，尤其是非常富裕家庭的孩子，依然更有可能被录取，正是这一观点让这项研究受到了如此多的关注。

sentences.en: And David, can you quantify the advantage that this study found?
sentences.zh: 大卫，你能量化这项研究发现的这种优势吗？

sentences.en: Walk us through some of the numbers that this study produced.
sentences.zh: 带我们了解一下这项研究得出的一些数据。

sentences.en: First, so the way that I find most helpful is when they look at a typical class at an Ivy Plus college, so those are the eight actual Ivy League schools,
sentences.zh: 首先，我认为最有帮助的方法是观察“常春藤+”大学的典型班级，也就是那八所真正的常春藤盟校，

sentences.en: plus Duke, the University of Chicago, Stanford, and MIT.
sentences.zh: 加上杜克大学、芝加哥大学、斯坦福大学和麻省理工学院。

sentences.en: When you look at the typical class at one of these colleges, about 9% of the students come from the top 1% of the income distribution,
sentences.zh: 当你观察这些大学的典型班级时，大约9%的学生来自收入分配前1%的家庭，

sentences.en: meaning they come from families earning more than $600,000 a year,
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们来自年收入超过60万美元的家庭，

sentences.en: and didn't get in because of their academic qualifications.
sentences.zh: 而且他们被录取并非完全是因为他们的学术资质。

sentences.en: Didn't get in because of their academic qualifications.
sentences.zh: 并非完全是因为他们的学术资质。

sentences.en: Or didn't get in solely because of their academic qualifications.
sentences.zh: 或者说，并非仅仅因为他们的学术资质而被录取。

sentences.en: These are still kids who do extremely well in school.
sentences.zh: 这些孩子在学校的表现依然非常出色。

sentences.en: But when you compare them to kids with less money who didn't get in, they don't do better.
sentences.zh: 但当你把他们与那些没被录取的贫困孩子相比时，他们的表现并不更好。

sentences.en: And in many ways, that is the core finding of the paper.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，这就是该论文的核心发现。

sentences.en: So David, let me make sure I understand this.
sentences.zh: 大卫，让我确认一下我是否理解正确。

sentences.en: This study finds that 9% of the college students enrolled in these highly selective elite colleges, in a sense, they don't deserve to have ever been admitted
sentences.zh: 这项研究发现，在这些高度选择性的精英大学中，9%的在校生在某种意义上，他们并不应该被录取，

sentences.en: and enrolled based on their qualifications versus any other kid who applied.
sentences.zh: 也不应该基于他们的资质与任何其他申请者相比而入学。

sentences.en: It's just that they were very, very rich.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是因为他们非常有钱。

sentences.en: I think the colleges would push back on that characterization.
sentences.zh: 我想大学会反驳这种说法。

sentences.en: Colleges would say, no, these students are still extremely qualified.
sentences.zh: 大学会说，不，这些学生依然非常优秀。

sentences.en: But I also understand why people would look at the study and make that statement.
sentences.zh: 但我也能理解为什么人们会看这项研究并得出这种结论。

sentences.en: Because if decisions were made based solely on academic qualifications, then 9% of the students at these schools wouldn't be there,
sentences.zh: 因为如果决策完全基于学术资质，那么这些学校里9%的学生就不会在那里了，

sentences.en: and they would be replaced by kids with similar academic qualifications who come from less affluent backgrounds.
sentences.zh: 取而代之的将是来自不那么富裕背景、但学术资质相似的孩子。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And there would therefore be greater economic diversity in these colleges.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些大学的经济多样性将会更高。

sentences.en: Precisely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And it gets even starker when you look at the richest of the rich.
sentences.zh: 当你观察最富有的人群时，情况就更明显了。

sentences.en: So let's imagine two different applicants with the same academic qualifications, one of whom comes from a family with average income,
sentences.zh: 让我们想象两个学术资质相同的申请者，其中一个来自平均收入家庭，

sentences.en: one of whom comes from a family with income in the top 0.1%.
sentences.zh: 另一个来自收入处于前0.1%的家庭。

sentences.en: So imagine a family making about $3 million or more a year.
sentences.zh: 想象一个年收入约300万美元或以上的家庭。

sentences.en: That applicant from the top 0.1% is more than twice as likely to be admitted than a child with the same test scores who comes from a family with an average income.
sentences.zh: 那个来自前0.1%家庭的申请者被录取的可能性，是来自平均收入家庭且考试分数相同的孩子的两倍多。

sentences.en: And I think it's that difference, this idea that even after a kid from a middle class or poor background has managed to do as well on the SAT, on these other academic measures,
sentences.zh: 我认为正是这种差异，即这种观念——即使一个来自中产阶级或贫困背景的孩子在SAT和其他学术指标上表现得同样出色，

sentences.en: they are still less likely to get in than a kid from a more affluent background.
sentences.zh: 他们被录取的可能性依然低于来自更富裕背景的孩子。

sentences.en: It's that that has people looking at this data and saying, how is that fair?
sentences.zh: 正是这一点让人们在看到这些数据时会问：这公平吗？

sentences.en: Right, because what this data establishes is that when it comes to college admissions, there really is a form of affirmative action for the nation's wealthiest kids.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为这些数据证实了，在大学录取方面，确实存在一种针对国家最富有孩子的平权行动。

sentences.en: Perhaps people suspected that was the case and maybe even acted as if it were the case, but here it is formally and pretty authoritatively documented and established.
sentences.zh: 也许人们怀疑情况如此，甚至表现得好像情况确实如此，但现在它被正式且相当权威地记录和证实了。

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: But David, as you've been talking, something's been bothering me, which is that a lot of these elite, highly selective colleges that we've been talking about
sentences.zh: 但大卫，在你谈话的过程中，有一件事一直困扰着我，那就是我们一直在谈论的许多精英、高度选择性的大学，

sentences.en: that this data is drawn from, they say, and they say it very proudly, that they are need-blind when it comes to admissions,
sentences.zh: 这些数据正是来源于此，他们声称，而且非常自豪地声称，他们在录取时是“需求盲目”的，

sentences.en: which means that technically speaking, they are not making admissions decisions based on income at all.
sentences.zh: 这意味着从技术上讲，他们根本不会根据收入做出录取决定。

sentences.en: In fact, they're supposed to be, as that phrase suggests, blind to it.
sentences.zh: 事实上，正如这个词所暗示的，他们理应对此“视而不见”。

sentences.en: So how does the study explain this level of advantage for those who are rich when the process is supposed to be blind to their financial background?
sentences.zh: 那么，当录取过程理应忽略财务背景时，这项研究是如何解释富人所享有的这种优势水平的呢？

sentences.en: What does it cite as the causes of it?
sentences.zh: 它指出了哪些原因？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's not wealth directly.
sentences.zh: 这并非直接与财富有关。

sentences.en: It's three other factors that correlate very much with wealth and end up giving wealthy kids an advantage.
sentences.zh: 而是另外三个与财富高度相关，并最终赋予富家子弟优势的因素。

sentences.en: And the first of those three will be familiar to many people.
sentences.zh: 这三个因素中的第一个，许多人会很熟悉。

sentences.en: It's called legacy admissions.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“校友子女优先录取”。

sentences.en: It's the idea that if one of the applicant's parents went to the same school, that applicant gets a leg up in the admissions process.
sentences.zh: 其理念是，如果申请者的父母之一曾就读于同一所学校，那么该申请者在录取过程中会获得优势。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's a formal process.
sentences.zh: 这是一个正式的流程。

sentences.en: It's not secret.
sentences.zh: 它不是秘密。

sentences.en: And it's been around for a long time.
sentences.zh: 而且已经存在很长时间了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's the official policy of most of these schools.
sentences.zh: 这是大多数此类学校的官方政策。

sentences.en: And of course, legacy students almost, by definition, are likely to be coming from well-off families.
sentences.zh: 当然，校友子女几乎在定义上就很有可能来自富裕家庭。

sentences.en: Not all of them, but many of them.
sentences.zh: 并非全部，但很多都是。

sentences.en: So this policy kind of guarantees a preference for a fair number of rich applicants.
sentences.zh: 所以这项政策在某种程度上保证了对相当一部分富裕申请者的优待。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The legacy population skews more affluent than the population as a whole.
sentences.zh: 校友子女群体比整体人口更偏向富裕阶层。

sentences.en: And this study tells us that legacy applicants get a leg up.
sentences.zh: 这项研究告诉我们，校友子女申请者确实获得了优势。

sentences.en: Now, it's nuanced.
sentences.zh: 当然，这很微妙。

sentences.en: And I think this surprises many people.
sentences.zh: 我认为这让很多人感到惊讶。

sentences.en: If you went to one of these schools and looked at the students, as this study did,
sentences.zh: 如果你曾就读于这些学校之一并观察学生，正如这项研究所做的那样，

sentences.en: the average legacy student has higher academic qualifications than the average non-legacy student, which again is a reflection of American inequality, right?
sentences.zh: 平均而言，校友子女学生的学术资质高于非校友子女学生，这再次反映了美国的不平等，对吧？

sentences.en: If you have a parent who went to one of these schools, you often will have had a better education growing up.
sentences.zh: 如果你有父母曾就读于这些学校之一，你通常在成长过程中会接受更好的教育。

sentences.en: And in fact, many of the most qualified students at these schools, the students who do the best, not only in college with grades,
sentences.zh: 事实上，这些学校里许多资质最好的学生，那些表现最出色的学生，不仅在大学成绩上，

sentences.en: but after college with the kind of graduate schools they go to or the jobs they get, they do really, really well.
sentences.zh: 而且在大学毕业后，无论是进入的研究生院还是获得的工作，他们都做得非常、非常好。

sentences.en: The issue is the colleges also admit a fair number of legacy students who are not there solely because of their academic qualifications,
sentences.zh: 问题在于，大学也录取了相当一部分并非仅仅因为学术资质而入学的校友子女，

sentences.en: but they're there because of a mix of their academic qualifications and their legacy status.
sentences.zh: 他们之所以在那里，是因为学术资质和校友身份的结合。

sentences.en: And what the researchers estimate is that about half of the legacy students at these schools wouldn't be there without the legacy advantage.
sentences.zh: 研究人员估计，这些学校里大约一半的校友子女学生，如果没有校友优势，就不会在那里。

sentences.en: One of the other things that the study shows, and we know this, is that the American elite comes disproportionately from these Ivy Plus schools.
sentences.zh: 这项研究显示的另一件事是，我们知道美国精英阶层不成比例地来自这些“常春藤+”学校。

sentences.en: And so the students who are being admitted are absolutely qualified in terms of a basic sense.
sentences.zh: 所以被录取的学生在基本意义上绝对是合格的。

sentences.en: Can they do the work?
sentences.zh: 他们能完成学业吗？

sentences.en: Do they have truly excellent academic outcomes in high school?
sentences.zh: 他们在高中是否有真正优秀的学术成果？

sentences.en: They do, including the half of legacy students who wouldn't be there without the booSt.
sentences.zh: 他们有，包括那半数如果没有这种助力就不会在那里的校友子女。

sentences.en: But the issue is that this is a scarce resource.
sentences.zh: 但问题在于，这是一种稀缺资源。

sentences.en: And what colleges are doing, the researchers argue, is they are concentrating opportunity among people who already get opportunity.
sentences.zh: 研究人员认为，大学所做的是将机会集中在那些已经拥有机会的人身上。

sentences.en: And that is something that is worth grappling with.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个值得深思的问题。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So that is legacy admissions as a force for reinforcing privilege in the admission system.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是作为强化录取系统中特权力量的“校友子女优先录取”。

sentences.en: What is the next factor that the study cites to explain how these schools are perpetuating privilege?
sentences.zh: 研究指出这些学校延续特权的下一个因素是什么？

sentences.en: I describe the second factor as private school polish.
sentences.zh: 我将第二个因素描述为“私立学校的润色”。

sentences.en: And that's the idea that the students who are applying from private schools, both day schools and boarding schools, so think of Andover, or in New York City, think of Dalton.
sentences.zh: 这就是说，那些从私立学校——包括走读学校和寄宿学校——申请的学生，比如安多福，或者在纽约市，比如道尔顿学校。

sentences.en: In Los Angeles, think of Brentwood.
sentences.zh: 在洛杉矶，比如布伦特伍德学校。

sentences.en: What happens is these schools are very good at making their students look good.
sentences.zh: 发生的情况是，这些学校非常擅长让他们的学生看起来很出色。

sentences.en: They're very good at writing teacher recommendations at these schools.
sentences.zh: 这些学校非常擅长撰写教师推荐信。

sentences.en: They're very good at helping the kids think about their essays.
sentences.zh: 他们非常擅长帮助孩子构思论文。

sentences.en: They're very good at helping the kids think about how to package their extracurriculars and to give them really great extracurricular options.
sentences.zh: 他们非常擅长帮助孩子思考如何包装课外活动，并为他们提供非常棒的课外活动选择。

sentences.en: So what ends up happening is that when colleges are faced with two applicants, again, let's imagine two with identical academic qualifications, test scores and grades,
sentences.zh: 所以最终的结果是，当大学面对两名申请者时，再次想象两名学术资质、考试分数和成绩完全相同的申请者，

sentences.en: one of whom comes from a public school and one of whom comes from a private school,
sentences.zh: 其中一名来自公立学校，另一名来自私立学校，

sentences.en: the private school applicant is more likely to get in than an equally qualified public school applicant.
sentences.zh: 私立学校的申请者比同样合格的公立学校申请者更有可能被录取。

sentences.en: And just to say something in defense of the admissions officers who are trying to make these decisions, sort through thousands of applicants of really insanely qualified teenagers,
sentences.zh: 顺便为那些试图做出这些决定、从成千上万名极其优秀的青少年申请者中进行筛选的招生官说句公道话，

sentences.en: they understand that private school polish exists, and they think they're able to control for it.
sentences.zh: 他们明白“私立学校的润色”是存在的，并且他们认为自己能够对此进行控制。

sentences.en: But actually, the polish is so effective that they can't or don't fully control for it.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，这种“润色”效果太好了，以至于他们无法或没有完全控制住它。

sentences.en: Well, David, let me push back against that defense because I want to better understand it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，大卫，让我反驳一下这种辩护，因为我想更好地理解它。

sentences.en: But admissions officers at these colleges, they know when a kid comes from a private school versus a public school.
sentences.zh: 但这些大学的招生官，他们知道孩子是来自私立学校还是公立学校。

sentences.en: It says so right on the application.
sentences.zh: 申请表上写得清清楚楚。

sentences.en: I went to Dalton.
sentences.zh: 我上的是道尔顿学校。

sentences.en: I went to Andover.
sentences.zh: 我上的是安多福学校。

sentences.en: So isn't this something that an admissions officer could actively seek to compensate for?
sentences.zh: 那么，这难道不是招生官可以主动去弥补的问题吗？

sentences.en: They can and they do.
sentences.zh: 他们可以，也确实在做。

sentences.en: They just don't do it as effectively as they think they do.
sentences.zh: 只是他们做得没有自己想象中那么有效。

sentences.en: So let's think about it this way.
sentences.zh: 我们换个角度来思考。

sentences.en: The applicant who is coming from a private school has teacher recommendations that really bring out exactly who that student is.
sentences.zh: 来自私立学校的申请者，他们的老师推荐信真的能精准地展现出这个学生到底是谁。

sentences.en: They have a guidance counselor recommendation that makes the kid feel like a full person.
sentences.zh: 他们有升学顾问的推荐信，让这个孩子看起来像个完整的人。

sentences.en: It's almost like a newspaper profile.
sentences.zh: 就像报纸上的人物专访一样。

sentences.en: The kid who's coming from public school is working with a guidance counselor who maybe has 150 or 200 kids for whom they have to manage that kid's high school to college process.
sentences.zh: 而来自公立学校的孩子，他们的升学顾问可能要负责150到200个孩子，要管理他们从高中到大学的整个过程。

sentences.en: The recommendation about the public school kid just doesn't pop off the page.
sentences.zh: 关于公立学校孩子的推荐信，读起来就没那么出彩。

sentences.en: Now, your skeptical question is absolutely fair.
sentences.zh: 现在，你提出的质疑非常合理。

sentences.en: Could they do it?
sentences.zh: 他们能做到吗？

sentences.en: They could.
sentences.zh: 他们能。

sentences.en: This study shows they're not.
sentences.zh: 但这项研究表明他们并没有做到。

sentences.en: Perhaps the best metaphor for this, as I'm hearing you describe this, is two identical products.
sentences.zh: 听你这么描述，最好的比喻或许是两个完全相同的产品。

sentences.en: We shouldn't think of two identical college applicants as products, but stick with me for a minute.
sentences.zh: 我们不该把两个一模一样的大学申请者看作产品，但请先听我说完。

sentences.en: Same quality, same qualifications, but one has a better package.
sentences.zh: 质量相同，资质相同，但其中一个包装更好。

sentences.en: And you're saying these college admissions advisors, they know that they should be thinking about the packaging, but it's so persuasive that they can't unsee it.
sentences.zh: 而你的意思是，这些大学招生顾问知道他们应该考虑包装的影响，但这种包装太有说服力了，以至于他们无法忽视。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And I should say, when we talk about private schools, that does not include religious schools, like Catholic schools.
sentences.zh: 我还要说明一点，当我们谈论私立学校时，这并不包括宗教学校，比如天主教学校。

sentences.en: So the private school bonus really applies to students who go to these independent schools,
sentences.zh: 所以，私立学校的加分项实际上适用于那些就读于独立学校的学生，

sentences.en: the private day schools, and the boarding schools that tend to be concentrated in places that also tend to be wealthier.
sentences.zh: 也就是那些私立走读学校和寄宿学校，这些学校往往集中在比较富裕的地区。

sentences.en: Okay, so that's private school polish.
sentences.zh: 好的，这就是私立学校的“润色”效应。

sentences.en: What is the third factor, according to the authors of the study?
sentences.zh: 根据这项研究的作者，第三个因素是什么？

sentences.en: The third factor is athletics.
sentences.zh: 第三个因素是体育运动。

sentences.en: And I think people understand that sports and recruiting are big parts of college admissions.
sentences.zh: 我想人们都知道体育和招生是大学录取的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: I don't think they understand quite how big they are.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他们并不完全了解这有多重要。

sentences.en: Or how sports interact with economic privilege.
sentences.zh: 或者说，体育运动是如何与经济特权相互作用的。

sentences.en: So how does it?
sentences.zh: 那它是如何作用的呢？

sentences.en: Well, I think if you said to someone, who tends to be on the sailing team, or the golf team, or the fencing team,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想如果你问别人，谁往往在帆船队、高尔夫球队或击剑队里，

sentences.en: they would say, oh, I assume it's kids who come from affluent backgrounds.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，哦，我猜是那些家境富裕的孩子。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But actually, it's almost every sport today that kids come from affluent backgrounds.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，如今几乎每项运动都是家境富裕的孩子在参与。

sentences.en: Some of the only exceptions happen to be the two highest profile sports, which is part of how I think our impressions are a little off here.
sentences.zh: 仅有的几个例外恰好是两项知名度最高的运动，这在一定程度上导致了我们的印象有些偏差。

sentences.en: They're football and they're basketball.
sentences.zh: 那就是橄榄球和篮球。

sentences.en: They're the sports that people watch on TV.
sentences.zh: 它们是人们在电视上观看的运动。

sentences.en: But if you look at almost any other sport, be it volleyball, be it soccer, be it baseball and softball,
sentences.zh: 但如果你看看几乎任何其他运动，无论是排球、足球、棒球还是垒球，

sentences.en: what has happened because of the rise of quite expensive, high-level travel sports in high schools,
sentences.zh: 由于高中阶段昂贵的高水平旅行运动队的兴起，发生了什么呢？

sentences.en: that even in these other sports, I don't think most of us think of baseball as a sport of the elite.
sentences.zh: 即使在这些运动中——我不认为我们大多数人会把棒球看作精英运动——

sentences.en: And yet, even in a sport like baseball, the kids who are playing at these colleges tend to come from quite affluent backgrounds
sentences.zh: 然而，即使在棒球这样的运动中，在这些大学里打球的孩子往往也来自相当富裕的家庭，

sentences.en: because that's who is able to do travel sports when they're young and then get so good at baseball
sentences.zh: 因为只有他们才有能力在小时候参加旅行运动队，并把棒球练得那么好，

sentences.en: that they can be good enough to play at one of these colleges as well as having the academic qualifications to get in.
sentences.zh: 以至于他们不仅能达到在这些大学打球的水平，还具备了入学的学术资格。

sentences.en: And how big a factor does the study say that sports and athletic recruitment are when it comes to reinforcing the privileges of the privileged?
sentences.zh: 那么，这项研究认为体育和体育特长生招生在巩固特权阶层的特权方面占多大比重？

sentences.en: They're big.
sentences.zh: 比重很大。

sentences.en: So if you look at one of these Ivy Plus schools and you look at the kids who come from the top 1% of the income distribution,
sentences.zh: 如果你看看这些“常春藤+”名校，再看看那些来自收入排名前1%家庭的孩子，

sentences.en: about one in every eight of those kids is a recruited athlete.
sentences.zh: 大约每八个孩子中就有一个是体育特长生。

sentences.en: So one in every eight of the very affluent kids at these schools is a recruited athlete.
sentences.zh: 所以，在这些学校里，每八个非常富裕的孩子中就有一个是体育特长生。

sentences.en: Compare that to lower-income or middle-income kids.
sentences.zh: 对比一下低收入或中等收入家庭的孩子。

sentences.en: Among those kids, only about one in 20 is a recruited athlete.
sentences.zh: 在这些孩子中，大约每20个人里才有一个是体育特长生。

sentences.en: So really, sports do skew quite affluent.
sentences.zh: 所以，体育确实明显偏向富裕阶层。

sentences.en: And as those numbers show, it's not just on the margins.
sentences.zh: 正如这些数字所显示的，这不仅仅是边缘现象。

sentences.en: It really is a meaningful part of the larger advantages to affluence in the admissions process.
sentences.zh: 它确实是招生过程中富裕阶层所享有的更大优势中重要的一部分。

sentences.en: It feels worth noting, David, that I think a lot of us not only didn't know that sports played this role in college admissions,
sentences.zh: 大卫，值得注意的是，我想我们很多人不仅不知道体育在大学招生中扮演了这样的角色，

sentences.en: but I think many of us, I'll just say I thought physical talent is physical talent.
sentences.zh: 而且我想我们许多人——我只想说我曾经认为——身体天赋就是身体天赋。

sentences.en: Speed is speed, right?
sentences.zh: 速度就是速度，对吧？

sentences.en: Agility is agility.
sentences.zh: 敏捷就是敏捷。

sentences.en: And that the best athlete, no matter class, no matter finances, would find their way to these colleges.
sentences.zh: 而且最好的运动员，无论阶层，无论经济状况，都能进入这些大学。

sentences.en: And that understanding or perhaps wishful thinking just turns out to be wrong.
sentences.zh: 那种理解，或者说一厢情愿的想法，结果证明是错误的。

sentences.en: Money actually does create better athletes.
sentences.zh: 金钱确实造就了更好的运动员。

sentences.en: Yes, it is just the case that we have so much inequality in our country that the better players in these sports tend to be the kids who come from more affluent backgrounds.
sentences.zh: 是的，事实就是我们的国家存在太多的不平等，以至于这些运动中表现更好的选手往往是来自更富裕家庭的孩子。

sentences.en: And there's something else going on here as well, which is to be a student athlete at one of these schools, you also have to clear a high academic bar.
sentences.zh: 这里还有另一层因素，那就是要成为这些学校的学生运动员，你还必须达到很高的学术门槛。

sentences.en: Now, it's not as high for any of the other categories we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 当然，这比我们谈论的其他任何类别的门槛都要低一些。

sentences.en: I mentioned before, legacy students have higher than average academic qualifications.
sentences.zh: 我之前提到过，校友子女的学术资质高于平均水平。

sentences.en: Athletes have lower than average academic qualifications at these schools.
sentences.zh: 而在这些学校里，运动员的学术资质低于平均水平。

sentences.en: But what they're doing is still kind of amazing, right?
sentences.zh: 但他们所做的事情仍然令人惊叹，对吧？

sentences.en: They are both really top athletes and they are truly excellent students.
sentences.zh: 他们既是顶尖运动员，也是真正优秀的学者。

sentences.en: So in the individual basis, I really want to emphasize this.
sentences.zh: 所以，从个人层面来看，我真的想强调这一点。

sentences.en: These students are incredibly impressive and accomplished people.
sentences.zh: 这些学生是非常令人印象深刻且成就斐然的人。

sentences.en: The issue is that when you look at it from a society-wide basis, this is a pattern that seems to be perpetuating advantage.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，当你从整个社会的角度来看时，这似乎是一种延续特权的模式。

sentences.en: So it's pretty obvious, David, from all this data, who most benefits from the three factors we just talked about.
sentences.zh: 所以，大卫，从所有这些数据来看，谁从我们刚才谈到的三个因素中获益最多，这很明显。

sentences.en: It's the rich and the super rich.
sentences.zh: 是富人和超级富豪。

sentences.en: Who, according to this study and all this data, is most disadvantaged by the power of the factors that we've just been talking about?
sentences.zh: 根据这项研究和所有这些数据，谁在刚才谈到的这些因素的影响下处于最不利的地位？

sentences.en: I think there are a couple different answers to that question.
sentences.zh: 我认为对这个问题有几种不同的答案。

sentences.en: And this is a really complex subject.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常复杂的主题。

sentences.en: If we restrict ourselves to the students who actually apply to these schools, the most disadvantaged is what we would call the upper middle class.
sentences.zh: 如果我们仅限于那些真正申请这些学校的学生，最不利的是我们所说的中产阶级上层。

sentences.en: It's the students from roughly the 70th percentile to the 95th percentile of the income distribution.
sentences.zh: 也就是那些收入水平大约在第70百分位到第95百分位之间的学生。

sentences.en: And so what happens is when the colleges are looking at students who all have the same academic qualifications,
sentences.zh: 所以发生的情况是，当大学在审视学术资质相同的学生时，

sentences.en: the biggest advantages go to the very wealthy kids for the reasons we've talked about.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所谈到的原因，最大的优势流向了非常富裕的孩子。

sentences.en: And the colleges also give an advantage, a smaller one, but still an advantage, to lower income kids.
sentences.zh: 大学也会给低收入家庭的孩子一些优势，虽然较小，但仍然是优势。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of people, including college leaders, would say that's appropriate.
sentences.zh: 我想很多人，包括大学领导，会说这是恰当的。

sentences.en: These kids have been running with wind in their face their entire lives, and they nonetheless excel.
sentences.zh: 这些孩子一生都在逆风奔跑，但他们依然表现出色。

sentences.en: Now, who that leaves out are the upper middle class kids, who they don't have the advantages of the very rich.
sentences.zh: 现在，被排除在外的就是中产阶级上层的孩子，他们没有超级富豪那样的优势。

sentences.en: They haven't overcome disadvantage like low-income kids have.
sentences.zh: 他们也没有像低收入家庭孩子那样克服过重重困难。

sentences.en: Think of a kid who maybe is not an athlete, not a legacy, and doesn't attend private school.
sentences.zh: 想象一个孩子，他不是运动员，不是校友子女，也不上私立学校。

sentences.en: So going to a big public school in a city or a suburb, and who's applying to one of these places.
sentences.zh: 他是在城市或郊区的一所大型公立学校上学，并且正在申请这些名校之一。

sentences.en: It is true that once that kid goes into the process, that kid is the least advantaged.
sentences.zh: 确实，一旦这个孩子进入录取流程，他就是最不占优势的。

sentences.en: And I think it's important to talk about that.
sentences.zh: 我认为谈论这一点很重要。

sentences.en: I would just be careful.
sentences.zh: 但我会谨慎一点。

sentences.en: It's not the case that upper middle class children growing up in America have less opportunity overall than poor children.
sentences.zh: 并不是说在美国成长的中产阶级上层子女，其总体机会就比贫困儿童少。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because we're already restricting ourselves to the children who apply to these schools.
sentences.zh: 因为我们已经把范围限制在申请这些学校的儿童身上了。

sentences.en: Poor kids have much less opportunity to do well in school.
sentences.zh: 贫困儿童在学校取得好成绩的机会要少得多。

sentences.en: Actually, even if they do well, they're less likely to apply to these schools than upper middle class kids are.
sentences.zh: 事实上，即使他们成绩优异，他们申请这些学校的可能性也比中产阶级上层的孩子低。

sentences.en: So depending how you look at it, you can either argue that poor kids are the most disadvantaged,
sentences.zh: 所以根据你看待问题的角度，你可以争辩说贫困儿童最不利，

sentences.en: or if you look at just the admissions process, you can argue that upper middle class kids are the most disadvantaged.
sentences.zh: 或者如果你只看招生过程，你也可以争辩说中产阶级上层的孩子最不利。

sentences.en: What's clear is that very wealthy kids, the top 1%, and particularly the top 0.1%, are the most advantaged.
sentences.zh: 显而易见的是，非常富裕的孩子，即前1%，特别是前0.1%的群体，是最占优势的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But just to linger for a moment on the upper middle class kids who are applying to college and hearing this conversation or hearing about this study,
sentences.zh: 但仅仅多停留片刻，谈谈那些正在申请大学并听到这段对话或听说这项研究的中产阶级上层孩子，

sentences.en: it may very much pain them and their families to discover that what they believed was an economic position that conferred opportunity
sentences.zh: 他们和他们的家庭可能会感到非常痛苦，因为他们发现自己曾经认为能带来机会的经济地位，

sentences.en: has, in terms of college admissions and enrollment, become a kind of disadvantage given the way the system is now constructed.
sentences.zh: 在大学录取和入学方面，鉴于目前的系统构建方式，已经变成了一种劣势。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think another way to think of that is that if the privileges for the top 1% in this process were to go away, the beneficiaries would not merely be low-income kids.
sentences.zh: 我认为另一种思考方式是，如果这个过程中前1%的特权消失了，受益者将不仅仅是低收入家庭的孩子。

sentences.en: In fact, some of the biggest beneficiaries for these large advantages for the very rich might be the merely affluent.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这些超级富豪所享有的巨大优势，其最大的受益者之一可能恰恰是那些仅仅是“富裕”的群体。

sentences.en: I think that if all colleges did were change their approach to private school polish, or all they did was get rid of legacy, or all they did was change their approach to athletics,
sentences.zh: 我认为，如果所有大学只是改变了对私立学校“润色”的处理方式，或者只是取消了校友子女优先录取，或者只是改变了体育特长生的处理方式，

sentences.en: we shouldn't assume that that would immediately allow a lot more low-income kids to come to these colleges.
sentences.zh: 我们不应假设这会立即让更多的低收入家庭孩子进入这些大学。

sentences.en: We shouldn't assume that it would allow a lot more underrepresented minorities to come to these schools.
sentences.zh: 我们不应假设这会让更多的代表性不足的少数族裔进入这些学校。

sentences.en: It would certainly make that easier by opening up more spots, but it wouldn't guarantee it.
sentences.zh: 这当然会通过腾出更多名额让情况变得更容易，但这并不能保证实现。

sentences.en: And so what happens on these college campuses is really going to depend on the full picture of what colleges do after the Supreme Court ruling.
sentences.zh: 所以，在最高法院裁决之后，这些大学校园里会发生什么，真正取决于大学所采取行动的全貌。

sentences.en: And how many of the systems that we've been talking about, they are willing to take on, fix, reform?
sentences.zh: 以及他们愿意承担、修复和改革多少我们一直在谈论的系统？

sentences.en: Change, yes.
sentences.zh: 改变，是的。

sentences.en: And one of the things colleges will tell you is that some of these things are harder to change, in their view, than many outsiders think they are.
sentences.zh: 大学会告诉你的一件事是，在他们看来，其中一些事情比许多局外人想象的要难改变得多。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜露。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times Games.
sentences.zh: 我编写了《Connections》游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏板块的谜题之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基，我每天负责创作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: Games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 游戏是由人制作的，就像你们刚才听到的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 今天就开始玩吧。

sentences.en: So, David, let's talk about why all these systems of advantaging the well-off, it turns out, are harder to change than we might think.
sentences.zh: 那么，大卫，让我们谈谈为什么所有这些让富人获益的系统，结果证明比我们想象的更难改变。

sentences.en: And I think we have to start with legacy admissions, which very much seems like low-hanging fruit if you want to reform the stuff we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们必须从校友子女优先录取开始，如果你想改革我们谈论的这些东西，这看起来非常像是唾手可得的果实。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, how do colleges think about legacy admissions, and why wouldn't they be pretty quick to just eliminate it?
sentences.zh: 那么，大学是如何看待校友子女优先录取的？为什么他们不能很快就直接取消它呢？

sentences.en: I think when a lot of people look at legacy, they say, how could this possibly exist?
sentences.zh: 我认为当很多人看校友子女优先录取时，他们会说，这怎么可能存在？

sentences.en: Part of the answer is, it's not something that colleges invented.
sentences.zh: 部分答案是，这不是大学发明的东西。

sentences.en: It's actually the norm in American society.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是美国社会的常态。

sentences.en: If you look around your company, there probably are people who work there whose parents also worked there.
sentences.zh: 如果你环顾你的公司，很可能有人在那里工作，而他们的父母也曾在那里工作。

sentences.en: If you think about Hollywood or the top singers, a strange percentage of them had parents who were in the same business.
sentences.zh: 如果你想想好莱坞或顶级歌手，其中有相当大比例的人，其父母也在同一行业。

sentences.en: Think about labor unions.
sentences.zh: 想想工会。

sentences.en: One of the main ways that people have gotten labor union cards over the decades, going way back to the early 20th century and the rise of unions,
sentences.zh: 几十年来，人们获得工会会员证的主要方式之一，追溯到20世纪初工会兴起时，

sentences.en: was because a plumber had a dad or an uncle or a brother who worked in that same union.
sentences.zh: 是因为水管工的父亲、叔叔或兄弟也在同一个工会工作。

sentences.en: That was legacy admissions for plumbers.
sentences.zh: 那就是水管工的“校友子女优先录取”。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And same for fire departments and police departments.
sentences.zh: 消防部门和警察部门也是如此。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: That's the way the world works.
sentences.zh: 这就是世界的运作方式。

sentences.en: Franklin D.
sentences.zh: 富兰克林·D·罗斯福就是一位“政治世家”出身的政客。

sentences.en: Roosevelt was a legacy politician.
sentences.zh: 温斯顿·丘吉尔也是。

sentences.en: So was Winston Churchill.
sentences.zh: 马丁·路德·金是一位“牧师世家”出身的牧师。

sentences.en: Martin Luther King was a legacy minister.
sentences.zh: 我想，尽管我们可以看着这些并说，等一下，这公平吗？

sentences.en: And I think, although we can look at that and we can say, wait a second, is that fair?
sentences.zh: 但当人们对一个机构有长期投入感时，它实际上具有巨大的好处。

sentences.en: It actually has enormous benefits when people feel a long-term investment in an institution.
sentences.zh: 它实际上具有巨大的好处。

sentences.en: We saw this during Trump's impeachment.
sentences.zh: 我们在特朗普弹劾案期间就看到了这一点。

sentences.en: Who were the Republicans willing to stand up and actually vote to convict Trump?
sentences.zh: 有哪些共和党人愿意站出来，真正投票给特朗普定罪？

sentences.en: Many political analysts pointed out.
sentences.zh: 许多政治分析人士指出。

sentences.en: They were people whose parents had been in politics.
sentences.zh: 他们都是父母曾从政的人。

sentences.en: Mitt Romney and Liz Cheney are legacy politicians who felt a larger commitment to the enterprise that made them willing to do something that was hard.
sentences.zh: 米特·罗姆尼和利兹·切尼是政治世家出身，他们对这一事业有着更强烈的使命感，这使他们愿意去做一些困难的事情。

sentences.en: Fascinating.
sentences.zh: 太迷人了。

sentences.en: This exists in a very real way for colleges.
sentences.zh: 对于大学来说，这种情况以一种非常真实的方式存在。

sentences.en: The people who are willing to volunteer their time, the people who attend sporting events of the college,
sentences.zh: 那些愿意贡献自己时间的人，那些参加大学体育赛事的人，

sentences.en: the people who volunteer in all kinds of ways and raise money for the colleges,
sentences.zh: 那些以各种方式做志愿者并为大学筹款的人，

sentences.en: the people who help make connections to help recruit a faculty member or help the college in some other ways,
sentences.zh: 那些帮助建立联系以协助招聘教职员工或以其他方式帮助大学的人，

sentences.en: are often people who don't simply feel a one-time connection to that school because they went there.
sentences.zh: 往往不仅仅是因为他们曾就读于那所学校，而对它产生了一次性的联系。

sentences.en: But they feel a multi-generational connection to the school.
sentences.zh: 而是他们对学校有着跨代际的联系。

sentences.en: And yes, fundraising is part of this.
sentences.zh: 是的，筹款是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: It absolutely is.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: It's an important part of it.
sentences.zh: 这是其中重要的一部分。

sentences.en: A family that has sent multiple generations to the same school, if that family happens to have someone who goes off and gets really rich starting a new company,
sentences.zh: 一个家庭如果有多代人就读于同一所学校，如果这个家庭恰好有人出去创业并变得非常富有，

sentences.en: they're much more likely to give money to that school.
sentences.zh: 他们就更有可能给那所学校捐款。

sentences.en: But I think people misunderstand it when they think of it as just a financial transaction, and they misunderstand it when they ask, why are colleges doing this?
sentences.zh: 但我认为人们把它仅仅看作是一笔金融交易是误解了它，当他们问为什么大学要这样做时，也是误解了它。

sentences.en: The answer is, healthy institutions in all kinds of realms of society tend to have people and families who feel a long-term connection to and investment in those institutions.
sentences.zh: 答案是，社会各个领域的健康机构往往都有对这些机构有着长期联系和投入的人和家庭。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So in the minds of these elite, highly selective colleges, there's a real and tangible virtue to legacy admissions that's, as you're saying, not just financial,
sentences.zh: 所以在这些精英、高度选择性大学的心目中，校友子女优先录取政策有一种真实且切实的优点，正如你所说，不仅仅是经济上的，

sentences.en: but cultural and institutional, despite the pretty clear ways in which it furthers the advantages of the rich.
sentences.zh: 而且是文化和制度上的，尽管它在很大程度上确实助长了富人的优势。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And let's also think about the way that these schools have changed.
sentences.zh: 让我们也思考一下这些学校发生的变化。

sentences.en: These schools have become a lot more diverse over the last several decades.
sentences.zh: 在过去的几十年里，这些学校变得更加多元化了。

sentences.en: So yes, legacy still disproportionately benefits white applicants, but with each passing year, it benefits white applicants less.
sentences.zh: 所以是的，校友子女优先录取政策仍然不成比例地使白人申请者受益，但随着时间的推移，它对白人申请者的好处在减少。

sentences.en: And the colleges will tell you, we have specifically heard from alumni of ours, alumni of color, who say to us, wait a second, you kept us out of your institution for centuries,
sentences.zh: 大学会告诉你，我们特别听到了我们的校友，有色人种校友的声音，他们对我们说，等一下，你们几个世纪以来一直把我们拒之门外，

sentences.en: and right after you let us in, you're going to get rid of a benefit that might let our children go here as well?
sentences.zh: 而在你们让我们进入之后，你们就要取消一项可能让我们的孩子也能来这里上学的福利吗？

sentences.en: Fascinating.
sentences.zh: 太迷人了。

sentences.en: That is another way in which the politics of this are quite complicated internally for colleges.
sentences.zh: 这是大学内部对此类政治问题感到非常复杂的原因之一。

sentences.en: So given all that, do we think that legacy admissions, however much people see it as contributing to all this privilege in the process, is likely to persist forever?
sentences.zh: 那么考虑到这一切，我们是否认为校友子女优先录取政策，无论人们多么认为它在这一过程中助长了所有这些特权，都有可能永远持续下去？

sentences.en: Not necessarily.
sentences.zh: 不一定。

sentences.en: The outcome here is genuinely uncertain, which is part of what makes this so fascinating.
sentences.zh: 结果确实是不确定的，这也是它如此迷人的部分原因。

sentences.en: Political pressure against legacy admissions really is rising.
sentences.zh: 反对校友子女优先录取政策的政治压力确实在上升。

sentences.en: Wesleyan University and Elite College in Connecticut just announced that they're getting rid of it.
sentences.zh: 康涅狄格州的卫斯理大学和精英学院刚刚宣布他们将取消这一政策。

sentences.en: The Biden administration just announced that it is launching a civil rights investigation of Harvard's use of legacy admissions.
sentences.zh: 拜登政府刚刚宣布，正在对哈佛大学使用校友子女优先录取政策展开民权调查。

sentences.en: We don't know what's going to happen, but I think it's fair to say that the legacy system is more vulnerable than it has ever been before.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道会发生什么，但我认为可以公平地说，校友子女优先录取系统比以往任何时候都更加脆弱。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: What are other ways that the colleges we've been talking about can mitigate against the advantages the study has identified?
sentences.zh: 我们一直在讨论的这些大学，还有什么其他方法可以减轻研究中发现的那些优势？

sentences.en: Well, there's one that's really counterintuitive, which is the SAT.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有一个非常反直觉的方法，那就是SAT考试。

sentences.en: We think of the SAT as perpetuating advantage because high-income kids do better than low-income kids.
sentences.zh: 我们认为SAT考试延续了优势，因为高收入家庭的孩子比低收入家庭的孩子表现更好。

sentences.en: White and Asian kids do better than Black and Latino kids.
sentences.zh: 白人和亚裔孩子比黑人和拉丁裔孩子表现更好。

sentences.en: But the question is, if colleges aren't going to use the SAT, and many of them are moving away from it, what are they going to use?
sentences.zh: 但问题是，如果大学不打算使用SAT，而且许多大学正在放弃它，他们打算用什么？

sentences.en: And this study suggests that they may end up using a set of factors that are actually more skewed than the SAT is.
sentences.zh: 这项研究表明，他们最终可能会使用一套实际上比SAT更具偏向性的因素。

sentences.en: So, essays and extracurricular activities and teacher recommendations are actually more skewed in favor of the affluent than the SAT is.
sentences.zh: 所以，论文、课外活动和教师推荐信实际上比SAT更偏向于富裕阶层。

sentences.en: And I think one of the things that this study suggests is that, yes, the SAT reflects a lot of inequality in our society.
sentences.zh: 我认为这项研究表明的一点是，是的，SAT反映了我们社会中的许多不平等。

sentences.en: But it also is a very good predictor of how students will do in college and after.
sentences.zh: 但它也是学生在大学及以后表现如何的一个非常好的预测指标。

sentences.en: It is an imperfect measure to be sure.
sentences.zh: 可以肯定的是，它是一个不完美的衡量标准。

sentences.en: Rich kids can take the test more than once.
sentences.zh: 富家子弟可以多次参加考试。

sentences.en: They can get private tutoring.
sentences.zh: 他们可以获得私人辅导。

sentences.en: But the benefits of all that stuff tends to be modeSt.
sentences.zh: 但所有这些东西的好处往往是有限的。

sentences.en: And if colleges want to identify really promising lower- and middle-income kids who can go there, there is no tool quite as reliable as the SAT, even though when they're using it,
sentences.zh: 如果大学想要识别出真正有前途的、可以去那里上学的中低收入家庭的孩子，没有比SAT更可靠的工具了，尽管当他们使用它时，

sentences.en: they need to remember that poor- and middle-class kids aren't likely to have quite as good scores as rich kids.
sentences.zh: 他们需要记住，贫困和中产阶级家庭的孩子不太可能像富家子弟那样取得那么好的成绩。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So, you're saying of all the gameable metrics that colleges currently rely on that have resulted in so much advantage for the rich, the SAT and the ACT, it might be, in a sense,
sentences.zh: 所以，你是说在大学目前依赖的所有可操纵的指标中，那些导致富人获得如此多优势的指标里，SAT和ACT在某种意义上可能是，

sentences.en: the least gameable test of someone's qualification, and therefore, colleges perhaps should be relying on it more than they are.
sentences.zh: 测试某人资格的最不可操纵的考试，因此，大学也许应该比现在更多地依赖它。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I know a lot of listeners will say, well, what about grades?
sentences.zh: 我知道很多听众会说，那么成绩呢？

sentences.en: And grades are a good measure.
sentences.zh: 成绩是一个很好的衡量标准。

sentences.en: The problem with using grades alone is we've had so much grade inflation in recent years, and there's so much inconsistency about what an A means at one high school than another,
sentences.zh: 仅使用成绩的问题在于，近年来我们出现了太多的成绩通胀，而且对于一所高中和另一所高中来说，A的含义存在太多的不一致，

sentences.en: that grades end up being really noisy.
sentences.zh: 以至于成绩最终变得非常嘈杂。

sentences.en: And so you're left with standardized tests as an imperfect measure, but maybe the least imperfect measure of all the options.
sentences.zh: 所以你只能把标准化考试作为一个不完美的衡量标准，但这可能是所有选项中最不那么不完美的衡量标准。

sentences.en: David,
sentences.zh: 大卫，

sentences.en: it feels like another way to fix this preference for rich applicants is for colleges to explicitly seek to take more applicants from public schools than from private schools,
sentences.zh: 感觉解决这种偏向富裕申请者偏好的另一种方法是，大学明确寻求从公立学校录取比私立学校更多的申请者，

sentences.en: given the private school polish problem established by this study.
sentences.zh: 考虑到这项研究确立的私立学校光环问题。

sentences.en: That feels highly achievable, and it feels like it would have a pretty big impact on the economic mix of students who attend these colleges.
sentences.zh: 这感觉非常可行，而且感觉它会对这些大学的学生经济构成产生相当大的影响。

sentences.en: Yes, I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为那是对的。

sentences.en: I think if colleges focus on the fact that right now they are disadvantaging many public school kids, they could fix this themselves through the admissions process.
sentences.zh: 我认为如果大学关注这样一个事实，即目前它们正在使许多公立学校的孩子处于不利地位，它们可以通过录取过程自行解决这个问题。

sentences.en: But there's a downside for these colleges whenever we're talking about them replacing affluent kids with much less affluent kids, which is affluent kids tend to pay full tuition.
sentences.zh: 但每当我们谈论这些大学用不太富裕的孩子取代富裕孩子时，它们都有一个缺点，那就是富裕的孩子往往支付全额学费。

sentences.en: Much less affluent kids do not.
sentences.zh: 不太富裕的孩子则不然。

sentences.en: They tend to receive large scholarships from the colleges.
sentences.zh: 他们往往会从大学获得大额奖学金。

sentences.en: And there are a few colleges out there that have such huge endowments that you might say, well, they don't need any of the tuition money.
sentences.zh: 有一些大学拥有如此庞大的捐赠基金，你可能会说，好吧，它们不需要任何学费收入。

sentences.en: But really, most of these colleges do not have endowments that are so big that they can simply ignore the tuition money.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，大多数这些大学的捐赠基金并没有大到可以简单地忽略学费收入的程度。

sentences.en: And the tuition money is so large that all of these colleges would need to find a way to make it up if they were to change their student population to admit fewer affluent kids and more lower- and middle-income kids.
sentences.zh: 而且学费收入如此之大，如果这些大学要改变学生群体，录取较少的富裕孩子和较多的中低收入孩子，它们都需要找到一种方法来弥补。

sentences.en: Now, it's important to say some colleges have done this.
sentences.zh: 现在，必须说一些大学已经这样做了。

sentences.en: Several colleges have become much more economically diverse over the last decade or so.
sentences.zh: 在过去十年左右的时间里，几所大学在经济上变得更加多元化。

sentences.en: One of them is Vassar College in New York, which does not have a truly enormous endowment.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是纽约的瓦萨学院，它并没有真正庞大的捐赠基金。

sentences.en: And so what Vassar did was it looked for other cuts to make to its budget.
sentences.zh: 所以瓦萨学院所做的是寻找其他可以削减的预算。

sentences.en: Its food wasn't quite as fancy as the food at other colleges.
sentences.zh: 它的食物不像其他大学的食物那么精致。

sentences.en: You can imagine that colleges might try to cut back on some of the really nice facilities that they now have for students.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象大学可能会尝试削减它们现在为学生提供的一些非常好的设施。

sentences.en: You can imagine that colleges would decide to cut back on the amount of administrators they have.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象大学会决定削减它们拥有的行政人员数量。

sentences.en: The number of administrators who work on college campuses has really soared in recent decades.
sentences.zh: 近几十年来，在大学校园工作的行政人员数量确实飙升。

sentences.en: So there are ways for colleges to find savings if they decide it is really a priority for them to admit and enroll more low-income kids.
sentences.zh: 所以如果大学决定录取和招收更多低收入家庭的孩子确实是它们的优先事项，它们是有办法找到节省开支的方法的。

sentences.en: They just have to decide what's a priority for them.
sentences.zh: 它们只需要决定什么是它们的优先事项。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And I feel like the big question that hovers over this conversation, and I want to end on it, is,
sentences.zh: 我觉得在这个对话中盘旋的一个大问题，我想以它结束，是，

sentences.en: based on your reporting, do you think these colleges want to make these kinds of changes and want to open up more spots for more economically diverse students?
sentences.zh: 根据你的报道，你认为这些大学想要做出这些改变，并想要为更多经济多元化的学生开放更多名额吗？

sentences.en: Because in talking to you, it becomes clear that the current system works in some ways for these highly selective schools, right?
sentences.zh: 因为在与你交谈时，很明显当前的系统在某些方面对这些高度选择性的学校是有效的，对吧？

sentences.en: It works for them financially to have lots of rich kids who pay full tuition.
sentences.zh: 拥有许多支付全额学费的富家子弟在经济上对它们是有利的。

sentences.en: It works for them in that legacy admissions reinforces their culture in ways that are tangibly beneficial.
sentences.zh: 校友子女优先录取政策在某种程度上强化了它们的文化，这在实质上是有益的，这对它们来说是有效的。

sentences.en: And let's be honest, big change is hard, and people may not want to undertake it.
sentences.zh: 老实说，重大的改变是困难的，人们可能不想承担它。

sentences.en: So I'm curious if you think the people who run these schools are deeply invested in getting rid of the three things we've been talking about,
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇你是否认为经营这些学校的人是否深切地致力于摆脱我们一直在谈论的三件事，

sentences.en: or if they're looking for ways to preserve them and maintain a status quo that functions pretty well for them, even if it's very unfair.
sentences.zh: 还是他们正在寻找方法来保留它们并维持一个对他们来说运作良好的现状，即使它非常不公平。

sentences.en: I've been interviewing college administrators about these subjects for 20 years now, and I think they are legitimately torn.
sentences.zh: 我采访大学行政人员关于这些主题已经20年了，我认为他们确实感到纠结。

sentences.en: The current system does have tangible benefits for colleges, as we've been discussing.
sentences.zh: 正如我们一直在讨论的那样，当前的系统确实对大学有切实的利益。

sentences.en: But the people running these colleges also care about their larger social mission, which is educating people to help run American society.
sentences.zh: 但经营这些大学的人也关心它们更大的社会使命，即教育人们帮助管理美国社会。

sentences.en: And they want those people to come from a very broad cross-section of backgrounds.
sentences.zh: 他们希望这些人来自非常广泛的背景。

sentences.en: And so we see these cross-currents right now, which is for the colleges, the current system has a whole bunch of advantages,
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在看到了这些交叉电流，即对于大学来说，当前的系统有一大堆优势，

sentences.en: and they have internal pressure from alumni groups and others to keep the status quo.
sentences.zh: 而且它们面临来自校友团体和其他人的内部压力以保持现状。

sentences.en: On the other hand, there is external pressure now coming onto these colleges to make changes.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，现在有来自外部的压力要求这些大学做出改变。

sentences.en: And I think they're trying to grapple with where do they end up with all of this?
sentences.zh: 我认为他们正在努力应对这一切最终会走向何方？

sentences.en: I think what many critics of the current system would say, including some of the researchers who did this paper, is they really have room to move toward more fairness.
sentences.zh: 我认为当前系统的许多批评者，包括做这项研究的一些研究人员，会说他们确实有空间向更公平的方向迈进。

sentences.en: Raj Chetty, who's a Harvard economist, is one of the people who did this research.
sentences.zh: 哈佛大学经济学家拉杰·切蒂是进行这项研究的人之一。

sentences.en: And what he said to me was, we don't need to put a thumb on the scale in favor of the poor.
sentences.zh: 他对我说的是，我们不需要把大拇指放在天平上偏袒穷人。

sentences.en: We just need to take the thumb off the scale that colleges, perhaps inadvertently, have put in favor of the rich.
sentences.zh: 我们只需要把大学可能无意中放在天平上偏袒富人的大拇指拿开。

sentences.en: Now, I don't think we know exactly what's going to change.
sentences.zh: 现在，我不认为我们确切地知道会发生什么变化。

sentences.en: But the fact that they have had a thumb on the scale in favor of the rich, and that we now know they have had a thumb on the scale in favor of the rich,
sentences.zh: 但事实上，他们曾经把大拇指放在天平上偏袒富人，而且我们现在知道他们曾经把大拇指放在天平上偏袒富人，

sentences.en: when you combine that with the politics of the Supreme Court decision, I think creates a lot of pressure on them to make some changes in response to the concerns that people have
sentences.zh: 当你把这一点与最高法院裁决的政治结合起来时，我认为这给他们带来了很大的压力，要求他们做出一些改变，以回应人们对以下问题的担忧：

sentences.en: about whether they are fulfilling the mission that colleges themselves say that they have.
sentences.zh: 他们是否正在履行大学自身声称拥有的使命。

sentences.en: Well, David, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好吧，大卫，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: In a dramatic court hearing on Wednesday, the judge overseeing what was expected to be
sentences.zh: 在周三一场戏剧性的法庭听证会上，负责监督预期中的

sentences.en: Hunter Biden's guilty plea to two federal tax charges put the proceedings on hold after a disagreement erupted between Biden's lawyers and prosecutors.
sentences.zh: 亨特·拜登对两项联邦税务指控认罪的法官，在拜登的律师和检察官之间爆发分歧后，暂停了诉讼程序。

sentences.en: The disagreement centered on whether Biden's plea, which involves no jail time, would protect him from future prosecution over his business dealings.
sentences.zh: 分歧的焦点在于，拜登的认罪协议（不涉及监禁）是否会保护他免受未来因其商业交易而受到起诉。

sentences.en: Biden's lawyers said that it would offer such protection, a prospect rejected by the judge.
sentences.zh: 拜登的律师表示，它将提供这种保护，这一前景遭到了法官的拒绝。

sentences.en: It was the latest twist in a case that has raised questions about whether Hunter Biden has been treated too harshly or too leniently because he is the president's son.
sentences.zh: 这是该案件的最新转折，该案件引发了关于亨特·拜登是否因为是总统的儿子而受到过严或过宽处理的质疑。

sentences.en: The Times reports that the judge could still approve the legal agreement in the coming weeks.
sentences.zh: 《泰晤士报》报道称，法官仍可能在未来几周内批准该法律协议。
